item.title: Canucks Rundown: Lineup Notes Vs. Flyers, Vancouver Mayor on Practice Facility
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Black Friday’s Canucks Rundown will preview the game against the Philadelphia Flyers and provide a practice facility update. Lineup Notes: Lankinen Could Return The Vancouver Canucks will face off against the Philadelphia Flyers in a Friday matinee game. The exact team deployment will be confirmed during warmups this afternoon in Philadelphia. There is reason to believe that Kevin Lankinen will get the start, following a tough outing for Leevi Merilainen , stopping 21 of 26 shots against the Detroit Red Wings on Wednesday . If Lankinen does start, it will be his first start since Nov. 3. Projected Lineup: DeBrusk-Chytil-Boeser Öhgren-Rossi-Lekkerimäki O’Connor-Mueller-Karlsson Reinhardt-Quillan-Cotter Buium-Hronek Pettersson-Willander Oleksiak-Schenn Lankinen A reminder that puck drop for Friday’s game will be at 1:00 p.m. PCT. Practice Facility Update Vancouver Mayor Pete Fry spoke to reporters on Thursday about Vancouver hosting the 2029 Grey Cup. During that press conference, Fry revealed that he would meet with the Canucks next week. One of the topics that will be discussed will be the much-awaited practice facility. Furthermore, The Province’s Patrick Johnston reported that Fry was interested in possibilities for a practice facility on Vancouver’s PNE grounds. Fry had been talking with minor hockey associations that have been lobbying for more ice rinks. Additionally, Vancouver Minor Hockey president Levi Higgs has suggested a practice rink be built north of the Pacific Coliseum, where a parking lot currently resides. It is located within the Hastings Park and PNE grounds. As a result, it sounds increasingly likely that the Canucks’ plans to use Britannia Rink as a practice facility will fall through. The Canucks are currently the only NHL team without plans for a practice facility. If there is a positive to take out of the season, getting the paperwork signed and sealed for a practice facility would be a great step in the right direction for the organization. item.title: Kovač puts Gadou hype into perspective after Arsenal heroics
item.description: Kovač puts Gadou hype into perspective after Arsenal heroics Following his summer move from RB Salzburg, Joane Gadou has quickly established himself as a regular starter at the heart of Borussia Dortmund's defence. Most recently, the 19-year-old delivered a standout performance in Wednesday's 1-1 draw with Arsenal, earning widespread praise and sparking reports that a number of top European clubs are keeping tabs on him. Dortmund head coach Niko Kovač, too, is pleased with Gadou's development, but is keen to stress that the youngster still has plenty to learn. "I've said it time and time again: learning week after week in the Bundesliga is one thing, but the learning experience of playing against the best in the world in this sport every three days is many times greater," Kovač said at a press conference on Friday. "He is developing well and, like everyone else, still has areas where he can improve. But it would be far too easy if we were to say that he was already the finished article. He's not. But where he is at the moment, he is helping us a great deal. "He will be given all the time in the world and all the support he needs. He works hard at learning, and I like that. When you're learning, you're allowed to make mistakes too." Gadou has made 17 appearances for Dortmund so far this season.

item.title: Jaissle on Newcastle star’s fitness ahead of Brighton
item.description: Jaissle on Newcastle star’s fitness ahead of Brighton Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle says Tino Livramento is closing in on a return to the starting XI but insists the club will not rush him back. The defender featured against Arsenal last weekend following his spell out with injury, although Jaissle says a decision on whether he is ready to start has not yet been made, ahead of the game against Brighton. “Always better when we need to make decisions when it comes to the starting XI,” Jaissle said. “Tino, for example, is on his way back but we need to see if he is ready to start. “We still have two days. I don’t want to rush something. “He is such a fantastic footballer, we need to be smart with him.” Lewis Hall has also trained this week having been forced off with cramp against Arsenal. But Joelinton remains unavailable, with Jaissle reluctant to put a timeframe on his return, though says he is optimic of a return “sooner rather than later”.

item.title: Chelsea ramp up interest in Como starlet Jacobo Ramon as Blues make definitive Benoit Badiashile transfer call
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED - AFP Chelsea are looking to Serie A to bolster their defence in 2027, with Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon emerging as a key target at Stamford Bridge. While the Blues have made a firm decision on Benoit Badiashile's loan spell at Napoli, securing Ramon's signature will require fending off fierce competition from domestic and European rivals. Chelsea plot Serie A defensive overhaul Chelsea are preparing to strengthen their backline in 2027, with their recruitment strategy strongly tied to Serie A. According to The Athletic , the Blues are closely tracking Como centre-back Ramon as they look to add defensive reinforcements. Despite their plans to bolster the squad at the back, Chelsea have no intention of cutting short Badiashile's loan spell at Napoli. The club have decided against recalling any of their first-team loanees during the January transfer window. Rising star Ramon attracts major interest Ramon has caught the eye of decision-makers at Stamford Bridge, where the Spaniard is strongly admired. His impressive progress in Italy was recently rewarded with his first senior call-up to the Spanish national team . Chelsea are not the only English club keeping a close watch on the defender's development. Premier League rivals Arsenal and Manchester United have also been linked with Ramon in recent weeks, pointing towards a potentially competitive race for his signature. Real Madrid hurdle and Badiashile's Napoli stint Any club hoping to prise Ramon away from Como will have to navigate a notable complication. Although he is formally a Como player, Madrid hold an option to re-sign him at the end of the season, mirroring the arrangement they have in place for his team-mate Nico Paz. Meanwhile, Badiashile remains in Italy after moving to Napoli on loan last summer with a €27 million option to buy. The 25-year-old French defender has made five appearances across all competitions this season. Badiashile's campaign was recently interrupted by an injury that sidelined him for several weeks. However, he has now returned to group training with the Serie A side. Summer window key for Chelsea's defensive plans Chelsea supporters will have to remain patient regarding any potential move for Ramon. While the club admire the Como centre-back, a deal would only be possible in the summer transfer window rather than mid-season. With no January recalls planned for Badiashile or any other first-team loanees, the Blues will keep their current loan arrangements intact for the rest of the campaign. Attention will then turn to the summer market, where the Blues' pursuit of Ramon - and the interest from Arsenal, Manchester United, and Madrid - will come into sharper focus.

item.title: Ex-Iceland goalkeeper Ingvar Jonsson who was part of Euro 2016 squad that stunned England dies aged 37
item.description: Ingvar Jonsson, the former Iceland goalkeeper who was part of the squad that defeated England at the 2016 European Championship, has died at the age of 37. His former club Víkingur announced his death on Thursday. The team did not provide a cause of death, although Jonsson had reportedly been diagnosed with cancer earlier this year. In a statement, the Icelandic club said: "It is with great sorrow and deep sadness that we announce that our dear friend and teammate Ingvar Jonsson, goalkeeper for Víkingur, passed away on Wednesday, November 25, in the arms of his loved ones." They added: "The club and all of Víkingur are thinking of his family and loved ones. We send them our deepest condolences." Jonsson served as an unused substitute during Euro 2016 , when Iceland created one of the greatest shocks in tournament history by knocking England out in the round of 16. The team were later eliminated by France in the quarter-finals. Iceland stunned England at Euro 2016 (Jonathan Brady/PA) (PA Wire) Paying tribute on X, European football’s governing body Uefa wrote: "We extend our deepest condolences to Ingvar’s family, friends and former team-mates. Our thoughts are with them at this difficult time." Jonsson earned eight international caps for Iceland, having made his first squad back in 2012. He had to wait another two years before making his first appearance for his country in a friendly against Belgium. His final cap for Iceland came in 2019, but he continued to make the squad through until 2022. His club career saw him start at Njardvik in his homeland before moving to Norwegian outfit IK Start in 2015. He would go on to play for Sandnes Ulf and Sandefjord prior to leaving Norway in 2018 to join Danish side Viborg. After two years in Denmark, Jonsson returned to Iceland to play for Vikingur and remained at the club until his passing.

item.title: Padres May Have Edge In Seiya Suzuki Chase
item.description: Free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki The San Diego Padres could use help in the outfield, and Seiya Suzuki makes sense as a target. Suzuki and Randy Arozarena are the two best hitters in free agency, and either one would be a great fit for the Padres. However, Arozarena reportedly prefers to sign on the East Coast. The Padres have reportedly shown interest in signing Suzuki, and according to Sanspo Japan , San Diego may have an edge over other suitors. "San Diego is one of the most comfortable environments for Seiya and his wife, Airi," a source told Sanspo Japan. Before Suzuki signed with the Chicago Cubs, the Padres were reportedly a potential landing spot for him. In fact, the Padres may have been his preferred choice. "If the salary and contract terms were the same for multiple interested teams, he would choose the Padres," a source told Sanspo Japan at the time. Suzuki has posted an OPS over .800 in each of the last four years, and was a great defender last year. He was a Gold Glove finalist, after defense had been a flaw in his game for years. The Padres could sign him to play right field and move Fernando Tatis Jr. to left field. They could also try to move Suzuki to left field, but it may not be wise to mess with his defense after he finally figured it out. item.title: Deportivo coach wary of Barcelona quality ahead of La Liga clash: ‘We are going to have to suffer a lot’
item.description: Deportivo coach wary of Barcelona quality ahead of La Liga clash: ‘We are going to have to suffer a lot’ Following a 4-1 win over Sabah in the UEFA Champions League, Barcelona will resume their La Liga campaign this weekend as they take on Deportivo de A Coruna. It promises to be a tricky affair for the Catalans, having made a long journey to Baku in midweek, forcing Hansi Flick to make multiple changes to the squad. Speaking ahead of the clash, Deportivo coach Antonio Hidalgo talked about the prospect of facing Barcelona and how the team has evolved under Flick. Hidalgo wary of Barcelona Hidalgo started by giving utmost respect to Barcelona, calling them among the finest while praising the standards instilled by Flick. “Surely comes one of the best teams in the world,” he said. “I think Hansi has taken them to a very high level of competitiveness. They’re showing it every week.” “They have won all their matches except one against Madrid and the Champions League against PSG and with an average of four goals per game,” he added. Hidalgo has immense respect for Barcelona. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) The Deportivo coach had no doubts about the challenge waiting for his players, as he demanded total commitment from his team. “We know that we are going to have to suffer a lot without the ball, be very tight. We have to be willing to suffer, to compete at the highest level in all duels and be very intense ,” he added. Hidalgo on Barcelona’s key threat Hidalgo went on to talk about the intensity Barcelona show when out of possession. He singled out that counter-press as a key threat for Deportivo de A Coruna. “We know of the aggressiveness that Barça has without the ball, it puts you a lot of difficulty, especially in that robbery after loss they do,” he said. Despite the challenge, Hidalgo backed his home fans to provide the atmosphere and inspire his players. “With our fans we will be much more powerful, we know it . You always come out with the conviction of competing for matches. “ We are First Division teams and everything is equal. It will be a game of a lot of tension and we will have to compete it at the highest level ,” he said. Aubameyang is expected to feature against former club Barcelona this weekend. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Hidalgo on Barcelona past and Aubameyang relief The match carries personal significance for Hidalgo, who spent his early years in Barcelona’s academy. “I’m from Barcelona, from Canovelles, which is half an hour away. I have my whole family there. From 12 to 21 years old, I was in the Barça quarry,” he said. “When you face teams from that entity, you always see them in a different and special way ,” he added. Finally, Hidalgo confirmed that Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, the former Barcelona forward, is fine after being left unharmed in a car crash ahead of the game. Source: Mundo Deportivo

item.title: Pochettino insists Manchester United must involve him in January transfer plans
item.description: Pochettino insists Manchester United must involve him in January transfer plans Mauricio Pochettino has said it is common sense for him to be involved in Manchester United 's recruitment plans. Manchester United are expected to invest in the January transfer window, as the club look to turn around their campaign. United are currently 19th in the Premier League table after 11 games. A centre-forward and additional defensive depth are understood to be on the agenda for the winter window, which will re-open on January 1, 2027. Pochettino was appointed as head coach on a two-and-a-half year deal this month, and was asked about potential signings on Friday. Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Brentford, Pochettino said it would make little sense for him not to be prominent in recruitment plans. "In the future of course, but right now we are focused on trying to relate all of the ideas to the squad," Pochettino said when asked how he will work with the club's leadership. "It's not common sense if the head coach is not involved in situations that affect the build up of the squad. For me, that is a benefit for Manchester United. If I am not involved, and I coach players that you don't know or maybe you don't want, or you don't agree, that is not for me. "I respect all ways to work but I am going to take my responsibility and everyone is going to know that I am going to be involved. That is what we were talking [about] in the last few days. "Being the coach is not only to pick 11 players. It's to assess and analyse the work behind about how you build. The responsibility is massive from the coaching staff." Manchester United have addressed one squad issue by activating a one-year extension in Bruno Fernandes' contract. Fernandes' deal was due to expire in the summer but has been extended until 2028.

item.title: Villanova’s Last Win Looking Worse, Wildcats With Another Chance Friday
item.description: Villanova rebounded from a bad loss against Pitt with a victory over, at the time No. 18, Michigan. At the time, the Wolverines were ranked and this looked like a good win. While it still will hold some weight on the resume, the early-season win has taken a hit. Michigan was blown out by Creighton just three days later and on Thanksgiving Day, trailed by nearly 30 against Miami. Safe to say, this is not the Michigan team that won a National Championship last season as the roster has turned over. Now, this just means that Villanova won a game it should have. The loss would have been even worse if the Wildcats were to get tripped up. Villanova will have another chance for a statement performance on the road against Kansas. This is the most difficult game that the team will play in the non-conference. Kansas has a dominant win over Kentucky this season with its only loss coming against No. 1 Houston. The game being played at Allen Fieldhouse provides another challenge for Villanova. As a 12-point underdog, an upset victory in a true road game against Kansas would catapult this team. item.title: ‘Would you approach LeBron James the same way?’ – A’ja Wilson’s agent calls out brands
item.description: Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A’ja Wilson’s agent, Jade-Li English of Klutch Sports Group, has opened up about pushing brands to recognise who Wilson is. A’ja Wilson just locked up a record fifth WNBA MVP, her third in a row, after putting up 26.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 1.9 blocks on 52.7% shooting, before the Aces ran into Golden State in the semifinals. While she’s making $1.4 million on the court with Las Vegas, Forbes estimates she’s pulling in over $5 million off it from deals with Nike, Chase, AT&T, and more, showing how big the gap can still be between WNBA salaries and star endorsement money. A’ja Wilson’s agent demands more from brands Even as A’ja Wilson ’s commercial pull keeps growing, her agent says getting brands to truly meet her at her level hasn’t always been simple, pushing companies to see who she is as a Black woman and measure every pitch against how they’d treat an icon like LeBron James . In a recent interview with Forbes , A’ja Wilson’s agent, Jade-Li English of Klutch Sports Group, said she has had to have “difficult conversations” with brands to make sure they “understand who she is as a Black woman.” English says she asks them, “‘Would you go to a LeBron James and approach a partnership with him the same way that you would approach A’ja Wilson?’” LeBron James is pulling in $85 million off the court this season, sitting fourth overall in NBA earnings at $88.9 million, with just $3.9 million coming from his salary. item.description: Kimi Antonelli secured his maiden F1 title in Mexico City earlier this month [Getty Images] World champion Kimi Antonelli headed Mercedes team-mate George Russell in first practice at the penultimate race of the season in Qatar. item.title: Fabrizio Romano: Liverpool ‘already discussing’ next steps under Andoni Iraola
item.description: Fabrizio Romano: Liverpool ‘already discussing’ next steps under Andoni Iraola Andoni Iraola Earning Liverpool Trust as Long Term Planning Begins Liverpool have moved quickly to stabilise the mood around Anfield, and the early signs under Andoni Iraola are encouraging. According to Fabrizio Romano, the club’s senior figures are pleased with what they have seen from the new head coach, and that matters because this is about more than a decent run of results. It is about direction, authority and whether Liverpool finally look coherent again. Romano’s key line was clear: “They are already discussing with Andoni Iraola about future plans and what they want to do. They are delighted with the coach and the coach is delighted with the Liverpool project. [He has] very good connections with the players.” That tells you two things. First, there is internal alignment. Second, this is not being treated as a short term fix. Liverpool Results Show Real Progress It has been close to six months since Iraola replaced Arne Slot, and the numbers are solid. Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League, just one point off second, they are well placed to reach the Champions League last 16 automatically, and they are through to the Carabao Cup quarter-finals. Add in penalty shootouts and he has won 12 of his first 18 matches, with only three defeats. Those figures do not prove anything on their own, but they do show competence, and after the chaos of the end of last season, competence is a serious improvement. Liverpool look sharper, more connected and more purposeful. There is structure in and out of possession, and there is less of the drift that damaged the side previously. Andoni Iraola Impact on Key Players The biggest positive may be individual improvement. Alexander Isak looks increasingly decisive, Florian Wirtz is influencing games with more regularity, and Alexis Mac Allister appears refreshed after a difficult end to the previous campaign. When Liverpool’s best players are performing like elite players, the whole team changes shape. This is where coaches earn credibility. Tactical ideas are fine, but players need to look better under your management than they did before. Right now, several Liverpool players do. That is why the praise from inside the club carries weight. Transfer Plans Already Point to Stability Iraola only signed a two-year deal, which raised eyebrows at the time. In reality, that suited his track record and suited a club that had just been burned badly. Shorter contracts can still produce long term thinking if both sides are convinced by the process. The fact discussions are already taking place over transfer plans for 2027 and beyond suggests Liverpool believe they have found a coach worth building with. That does not guarantee anything by spring. Football moves fast, and reputations collapse quickly when results turn. But for now, Liverpool have a head coach improving players, collecting wins and restoring order. That is a very good start.

item.title: The Anaheim Ducks Are Getting One Of The NHL’s Most Exciting Young Forwards Back
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cutter Gauthier’s historic November has received plenty of attention, but the Anaheim Ducks have another 22-year-old or younger forward producing at better than a point-per-game pace this season. Beckett Sennecke is expected to return to the Ducks’ lineup Friday against the Los Angeles Kings after missing three games with an upper-body injury. Head coach Joel Quenneville confirmed Thursday that Sennecke is ready to return, according to Zach Cavanagh of The Sporting Tribune. The 20-year-old has scored 12 goals and registered 14 assists through 22 games this season after finishing third in Calder Trophy voting with 23 goals and 60 points in 82 games last season. He’s nearly doubled his goal-scoring rate and is on pace for 99 points over a full 84-game schedule. Less than three years ago, Sennecke was playing junior hockey with the Oshawa Generals. He’s now producing at a rate that would’ve put him among the NHL’s leading scorers in most seasons. Sennecke has some ridiculous puck skills, and 10 of his 12 goals this season have come from high-danger areas. According to NHL EDGE, that ties him with Auston Matthews for second in the league, just one behind Artturi Lehkonen. He’s also been on the ice for 22 power-play goals, one fewer than Gauthier. The Ducks lead the NHL with a 33.7% power play, and Sennecke was back practicing with the first unit Thursday. With Leo Carlsson sidelined by an upper-body injury, NHL.com has Sennecke projected to play alongside Gauthier and Roger McQueen on Friday. That’s three forwards selected inside the top 10 of their respective drafts, none of whom are older than 22. McQueen, the 10th overall pick in 2025, scored against the San Jose Sharks on Wednesday and could benefit from playing between two of the league’s most productive young wingers. There aren’t many better linemates for a young center trying to establish himself offensively in the NHL right now. The Ducks lost consecutive 3-2 games against the Utah Mammoth and Seattle Kraken in Sennecke’s absence before beating San Jose 7-0 on Wednesday. They enter Friday’s game with a 12-13-1 record despite the offensive production they’ve been getting from their young forwards. Anaheim has two games against Los Angeles this weekend, and with Carlsson still out, Quenneville could give us our first extended look at what Gauthier, McQueen and Sennecke can do together. item.title: A Tale of Two Kickers on Thanksgiving Night
item.description: William Purnell-Imagn Images Thanksgiving night in Buffalo turned into a tale of two kickers , and only one delivered. While the headlines promised a battle between Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, the real story ended with Harrison Butker missing a 46-yard attempt and Tyler Bass hitting a 57-yard winner as time expired. The Bills beat the Chiefs 13-10 in the rain, a result that feels like a slap in the face for Kansas City’s special teams unit. Butker has been a disappointment this season, missing eight field goals in 2026. That total is tied for the most in the league (or leads, depending on whether extra-point misses are included). He hasn’t made a single kick exceeding 50 yards this year, rendering his rainy-night failure predictable instead of shocking. Meanwhile, Bass has been nearly perfect, going 26-for-27 this season. The performance gap was more than one bad night; it was a season-long trend that finally caught up with the Chiefs. Chiefs coach Andy Reid said after the loss that he wasn’t ready to say whether Butker will remain the kicker in Kansas City . “I’ll go back and go through all of it again,” Reid said immediately after the game. He added, “Not gonna make any decisions right this minute.” This hesitation is baffling when you look at the numbers. Since a kicker must successfully make his kicks, Butker is simply failing to perform. The Chiefs had other chances to win, but special teams issues cost them. A controversial call wiped out a huge catch by Rashee Rice, and a fumbled snap by Mahomes derailed a late drive. Yet, the missed field goal by Butker loomed large. Bills Climb While Chiefs Stumble Securing this victory puts Buffalo at 10-1, maintaining their position in the driver’s seat for the AFC’s No. 1 seed. The Chiefs fell to 8-3, now half a game behind the Denver Broncos in the AFC West. Weather played a part, with freezing rain and wind making conditions nasty for everyone. Josh Allen struggled through one of his poorest passing games, while Mahomes managed 174 yards but could not secure the win. James Cook ran for 117 yards and scored the only touchdown for Buffalo, but the game was ultimately decided by the feet. The Bills overcame a sluggish offense to win on the special teams play of the year. Traveling to Los Angeles to play the Rams next Thursday night means the Chiefs will receive no additional rest.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
